title: HARBOUR ROAD SELF STORAGE: UNIT RENTAL AGREEMENT
summary: This is a rental of storage space at Harbour Road Self Storage, month to month after an initial part month, at the rent on the Unit Schedule. Signing commits you to a rental that renews on the first of every month on its own, rent the Operator can raise on thirty days notice, a late charge and an administration charge set in a schedule posted at the facility, and rules and terms the Operator can change by posting them. What the Operator can owe you for loss or damage to what you store is capped at five thousand dollars even where the Operator was negligent, third party claims connected to your unit fall on you, and unpaid rent gives the Operator a lien over everything inside.

plantedClauses.sourceSentence: After the initial term this Agreement continues on a month to month basis, each month renewing on the first day of the month without notice from either party, until it is ended as Section 8 describes.
plantedClauses.consequence: After the first part month the rental renews itself on the first of every month. Nobody sends a notice and nobody asks, and it carries on until one side ends it the way Section 8 sets out.

exit.text: Give written notice at least ten days before the end of a month, take everything out and sweep the unit. Rent already paid for the month you move out in is not refunded.
exit.sourceSentence: The Occupant may end this Agreement by giving written notice at least ten days before the end of a month, removing all property and leaving the unit swept clean.

plantedClauses.why: Baseline high for auto-renewal and held there: the way out is ten days notice before month end, which is shorter than a window a reader who has not read the clause could use.

plantedClauses.sourceSentence: The Operator may increase the monthly rent on not less than thirty (30) days written notice to the Occupant, and the increased rent is due on the first rent day falling after the notice period ends.
plantedClauses.consequence: The Operator can put your rent up with thirty days written notice. The higher rent is due on the first rent day after the notice period runs out.
plantedClauses.why: Moderate: it costs money and the reader can still move out. No cap on the size of an increase and no limit on how often one can be given.

plantedClauses.sourceSentence: Rent not received by the sixth day of the month incurs the late charge shown in the Schedule of Charges posted in the ofﬁce and on the Harbour Road website, and each further notice the Operator is required to send about an unpaid balance incurs the administration charge shown in the same schedule.
plantedClauses.consequence: Rent that arrives after the fifth of the month triggers a late charge, and every reminder letter about an unpaid balance triggers an administration charge. Neither figure is in this agreement: both sit in a Schedule of Charges posted at the facility, which Section 6 lets the Operator change.
plantedClauses.why: Moderate: costs, not a lost lever. Both figures are cross-referenced out of the document. The sentence carries an fi ligature glyph, which is the character class that broke a citation in the ticket 10 run.

plantedClauses.sourceSentence: The Operator's total liability to the Occupant for any loss of or damage to stored property, however caused, including loss or damage caused by the Operator's own negligence, is limited to five thousand dollars ($5,000) unless the Occupant has declared a higher value on the Unit Schedule and paid the corresponding value protection fee.
plantedClauses.consequence: If what you store is lost or damaged, including when the Operator caused it by their own carelessness, the most you can recover is five thousand dollars. Getting a higher figure means having declared a value on the Unit Schedule and paid the value protection fee.
plantedClauses.why: High: the claim survives and the payout is capped, and the cap is stated flat rather than by cross-reference, which is the readable version of this clause. It sweeps in the Operator's own negligence.

plantedClauses.sourceSentence: The Occupant will indemnify, defend and hold the Operator harmless from every claim, demand, loss, cost and expense, including reasonable attorney fees, brought by any person and arising out of the Occupant's use of the unit or the premises, the property stored in the unit, or the acts of anyone the Occupant allows on to the premises.
plantedClauses.consequence: If anyone brings a claim connected to your unit, what is in it, or someone you let on to the site, you pay the Operator's costs and legal fees.
plantedClauses.why: High: one way, no cap, no carve-out, and the trigger reaches the conduct of anyone the reader brings along.

plantedClauses.sourceSentence: Gate hours, the rules posted in the office, and the terms of this Agreement may be changed by the Operator on notice posted at the facility and sent to the Occupant's last known email address, and the changed version applies to the Occupant from the first day of the month after it is posted.
plantedClauses.consequence: The Operator can change the gate hours, the site rules and the terms of this agreement by posting a notice and emailing your last known address. The changed version applies to you from the first of the following month.
plantedClauses.why: Critical: it reaches the terms of the agreement itself and needs no agreement from the reader. Notice goes to a last known address rather than a confirmed one.
